data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only when the test's failure mode is not already enumerated in the subject's own error vocabulary; the 1-of-9 loss is a mutation that changed the error vocabulary itself, so compile.py's shown-to-fail-first installation could not find a failing test because the failure was unnameable.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the lost mutation was a content-edit hole not affecting any error name, the vocabulary mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the ordinarily-guarded modules' guards are written in terms of structural patterns rather than named errors, the vocabulary-dependence claim is unsupported.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py's mutation operators do not include error-name renames, the 1/9 loss cannot be attributed to vocabulary change.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The subject constrains itself through an error vocabulary (e.g. INV-value-vocabulary, INV-replay-fold). A test that asserts on a specific error name describes the vocabulary. A mutation that alters the vocabulary (e.g. renames an error, changes a selector) is not constrained by any test because the test's assertion references the old name. The distribution 3-of-26 vs 1-of-9 reflects the ratio of vocabulary-stable mutations to vocabulary-altering mutations across modules.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
